findings.summary: db.drafts.put is invoked as a side effect inside the setSets functional updater, violating React's requirement that state updater functions be pure.
findings.mechanism: React (in StrictMode/dev, and potentially under concurrent-rendering replay) may invoke a functional setState updater more than once per logical update. Each invocation fires a real IndexedDB write via db.drafts.put with a freshly computed updatedAt timestamp. The put is keyed by id so content converges to the same value, but every tap now issues extra, unawaited Dexie writes as a side effect of state resolution rather than of a committed render — an anti-pattern that risks redundant writes (and, in the rarer case of a synchronous Dexie validation error, an exception thrown mid-updater that aborts the state update entirely, unlike the previous sequential writeThrough where the setSets call had already succeeded before the write was attempted).
